summary: Shared pure helpers for the work-store adapters: constants, the canonical intent digest, timestamp/title shaping, actor JSON, and the project/lock/notify primitives. All helpers are pub(crate).
responsibilities: work_err maps AdapterError to WorkError::store with the error's Display text.

intent_digest is Python's sha256_canonical: SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON encoding - object keys sorted ascending, no spaces, non-ASCII emitted as raw UTF-8. Implement a small recursive writer over the Value (sort object keys yourself; do not rely on serde_json Map ordering).
format_ts is Python's _timestamp: UTC ISO-8601 with a Z suffix; seconds precision when the microsecond component is 0, else exactly 6 fractional digits.

prepare_title is work_config.prepare_title: first non-blank line of the prompt, whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces, truncated to 128 chars and to 512 UTF-8 bytes (dropping whole chars), right-trimmed; an empty result is rejected(400, invalid_request).
actor_json builds {"kind": kind.as_str(), "id": id}; parse_actor reads payload.actor back into an Actor (None when absent or malformed).
require_project returns rejected(403, denied) when the alias is not in the store's allowed projects.
advisory_lock runs SELECT pg_catalog.pg_advisory_xact_lock(pg_catalog.hashtextextended($1::text, $2::bigint)) with the scope string "{owner}\n{project_alias}" and ADVISORY_LOCK_SALT.
notify runs SELECT pg_catalog.pg_notify($1, '') with NOTIFY_CHANNEL.
invariants: Every helper is pub(crate); tokio_postgres::Row never appears in a public signature.
The canonical digest writer sorts keys at every object depth; arrays keep order; strings are JSON-escaped exactly as serde_json escapes them (use serde_json::to_string on each string scalar).
